akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلْقُوَىٰ﴾: the plural of "القُوَّةِ" (strength). Some Arabs say "حُبْوَة" and "حِبَى", so by this analogy one should say "القِوى". Some Arabs say "رِشْوَة" and "رُشا" (bribe), and some say "رُشْوة" and "رِشا". Some Arabs say "صُوَرٌ" and "صِوَرٌ" (forms), and the good one is "صُوَر": ﴿صَوَّرَكُـمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُـمْ﴾, and ﴿صِوَرَكُـمْ﴾ is (also) read.

akhfash:19-19.t: Some read ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ ٱللاَّتَ وَٱلْعُزَّىٰ﴾; when you pause you say "اللاَّة", and likewise "مَنَاةَ": you say "مَنَاهْ". Some read ﴿ٱللاَّتَ﴾ (with doubled tāʾ), making it from "اللاتِّ": the one who kneads (يَلُتّ). It is a dialect of the Arabs to pause on words that have hāʾ with tāʾ; they say "رأيتُ طَلْحَتْ" (I saw Ṭalḥa). Everything in the Quran written with tāʾ, you pause on it only with tāʾ, as in ﴿نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ and ﴿شَجَرَةَ ٱلزَّقُّومِ﴾.

akhfash:37-38.t: And He said ﴿وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلَّذِي وَفَّىٰ﴾ ﴿أَلاَّ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ﴾: His word ﴿أَنْ لاَ تِزَرُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ﴾, i.e. "that no bearer of burdens bears…" (بِأَنْ لا تَزِرُ).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالنَّجْمِ﴾ the Pleiades, ﴿إِذَا هَوَى﴾ when it set,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ﴾ Muhammad, upon him be blessing and peace, from the path of guidance, ﴿وَمَا غَوَى﴾ he has not been involved in error, which is ignorance arising from a corrupt belief;

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمَا يَنْطِقُ﴾ in what he brings you ﴿عَنِ الْهَوَى﴾ from the desire of his own self;

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ (meaning: not) ﴿هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى﴾ to him.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿ذُو مِرَّةٍ﴾ of strength and power, or of fine appearance, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him; ﴿فَاسْتَوَى﴾ he settled,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلَى﴾ the horizon of the sun, that is, at its rising place, in his form in which he was created. The Prophet ﷺ saw him while he was at Ḥirāʾ; he had blocked the horizon as far as the west, and he fell down in a swoon. He had asked him to show himself in the form in which he was created, so he made an appointment with him at Ḥirāʾ; then Gabriel came down to him in the form of human beings.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ دَنَا﴾ he drew near to him, ﴿فَتَدَلَّى﴾ he came even nearer,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَكَانَ﴾ from him ﴿قَابَ﴾ the measure of ﴿قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى﴾ than that, until he recovered and his fright subsided.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَأَوْحَى﴾ He, Exalted is He, ﴿إِلَى عَبْدِهِ﴾ Gabriel, ﴿مَا أَوْحَى﴾ Gabriel to the Prophet ﷺ; and the content of the revelation is not mentioned, to magnify its importance.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿مَا كَذَبَ﴾ with the light and the doubled [dhāl]: did not deny ﴿الْفُؤَادُ﴾ the heart of the Prophet ﴿مَا رَأَى﴾ with his eyes, of the form of Gabriel.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾ do you dispute with him and try to overcome him ﴿عَلَى مَا يَرَى﴾? An address to the idolaters who denied the Prophet's ﷺ seeing Gabriel.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ﴾ in his form ﴿نَزْلَةً﴾ one time ﴿أُخْرَى﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ when he was taken on the Night Journey through the heavens; it is a lote tree to the right of the Throne, beyond which none of the angels or others passes.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿عِنْدَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى﴾ to which the angels and the spirits of the martyrs and the God-fearing resort.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ when ﴿يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَى﴾ of birds and other things; and إِذْ is governed (maʿmūla) by رَآهُ.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ﴾ of the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَمَا طَغَى﴾ that is, his sight did not swerve from what it was meant to see, nor go beyond it, that night.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿لَقَدْ رَأَى﴾ in it ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرَى﴾ that is, the great ones, that is, some of them: he saw, of the wonders of the unseen dominion, a green cushion (rafraf) that blocked the horizon of the sky, and Gabriel having six hundred wings.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the discussion follows in the next entry.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَمَنَاةَ الثَّالِثَةَ﴾ to the two before it, ﴿الْأُخْرَى﴾ an adjective of disparagement for the third. They are idols of stone that the idolaters used to worship, claiming that they would intercede for them with Allah. The first mafʿūl (object) of أَرَأَيْتُمُ is اللَّاتَ and what is conjoined to it, and the second is omitted. The meaning is: tell me, do these idols have power over anything at all, so that you worship them instead of Allah, who has power over what was mentioned before? And since they also claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah, despite their dislike of daughters, there was revealed:

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى﴾ unjust; from ضَازَهُ يَضِيزُهُ, when he wronged him and was unjust to him.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِنْ هِيَ﴾ that is, the things mentioned are not ﴿إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا﴾ that is, with which you have named, ﴿أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ﴾ idols that you worship; ﴿مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا﴾ that is, for worshipping them, ﴿مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ any argument or proof. ﴿إِنْ﴾ (meaning: not) ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ in worshipping them ﴿إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ﴾ of what Satan has made fair-seeming to them, namely that they will intercede for them with Allah the Exalted; ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدَى﴾ on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, with decisive proof, yet they did not turn back from what they were upon.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَمْ لِلْإِنْسَانِ﴾ that is, for every human being among them, ﴿مَا تَمَنَّى﴾ namely that the idols will intercede for them? The matter is not so.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى﴾ that is, this world; so nothing happens in either of them except what He, Exalted is He, wills.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ﴾ that is, and many of the angels ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ — and how honoured they are with Allah — ﴿لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ﴾ to them in it ﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ of His servants ﴿وَيَرْضَى﴾ with him, because of His words {وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى}; and it is known that it does not come from them except after permission for it: {مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ}.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثَى﴾ in that they said: they are the daughters of Allah.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ بِهِ﴾ in this saying ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ﴾ (meaning: not) ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ in it ﴿إِلَّا الظَّنَّ﴾ which they have imagined; ﴿وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا﴾ that is, in place of knowledge, in matters where knowledge is what is required.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ تَوَلَّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا﴾ that is, the Quran, ﴿وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — and this was before the command to fight (jihād).

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, seeking this world, ﴿مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ that is, the limit of their knowledge: that they preferred this world to the Hereafter. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدَى﴾ that is, He knows both and will recompense both.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ that is, He is the Owner of that, and among it are the one astray and the one rightly guided; He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاؤُا بِمَا عَمِلُوا﴾ of idolatry and other things, ﴿وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا﴾ by affirming His oneness and other acts of obedience, ﴿بِالْحُسْنَى﴾ that is, Paradise. And He described the doers of good with His words:

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ﴾ it is the minor sins, such as the glance, the kiss and the touch; so it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and the meaning is: but the minor sins are forgiven through avoiding the major ones. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ through that and through accepting repentance. And concerning those who used to say "our prayer, our fasting, our pilgrimage" there was revealed: ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ (meaning: knowing) ﴿بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ that is, He created your father Adam from dust, ﴿وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ﴾ plural of جَنِينٍ (foetus), ﴿فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ do not praise yourselves, that is, by way of self-admiration; but by way of acknowledging the blessing it is good. ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ that is, knowing ﴿بِمَنِ اتَّقَى﴾

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى﴾ from faith, that is, apostatised when he was reproached for it and said "I feared Allah's punishment"; so the one who reproached him guaranteed to bear Allah's punishment for him if he returned to his idolatry, and to give him such-and-such of his wealth; so he returned,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَأَعْطَى قَلِيلًا﴾ of the wealth named ﴿وَأَكْدَى﴾ withheld the rest; taken from الْكُدْيَةِ, which is hard ground like rock that stops the well-digger from digging when he reaches it.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَى﴾ does he know, as part of it, that another will bear the punishment of the Hereafter for him? No. He was al-Walīd ibn Mughīra, or someone else. The clause أَعِنْدَهُ is the second mafʿūl (object) of رَأَيْتَ in the sense of "tell me".

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ (meaning: rather) ﴿لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَى﴾ the books of the Torah, or scrolls before it,

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the scrolls of ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى﴾ fulfilled what he was commanded, as in {وَإِذِ ابْتَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ}; and the explanation of مَا [is]:

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى﴾ etc. And أَنْ is lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), that is: that no soul bears the sin of another,

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ (meaning: that it is so that) ﴿لَيْسَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى﴾ of good; so he has nothing of the good from another's striving,

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَى﴾ that is, will be seen in the Hereafter,

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى﴾ the most complete. One says جَزَيْتُهُ سَعْيَهُ and بِسَعْيِهِ (I recompensed him [for] his striving).

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ with fatḥa, as a conjunction [to what precedes]; and it has been read with kasra, as a resumptive clause; and likewise what comes after it. So on the second [reading] the content of the clauses is not [part of what is] in the scrolls. ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ the return and the destination after death, and He will recompense them;

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ﴾ whom He wills: He made him glad, ﴿وَأَبْكَى﴾ whom He wills: He made him sad;

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ﴾ in this world ﴿وَأَحْيَا﴾ for the resurrection;

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ the two kinds, ﴿الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى﴾

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ semen ﴿إِذَا تُمْنَى﴾ when it is poured into the womb;

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشَاءَةَ﴾ with the long and the short vowel [النَّشْأَةَ], ﴿الْأُخْرَى﴾ the other creation, for the resurrection, after the first creation;

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى﴾ people, by sufficiency through wealth, ﴿وَأَقْنَى﴾ gave wealth that is kept as a possession;

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَى﴾ it is a star behind Orion (al-Jawzāʾ), which used to be worshipped in the Jāhiliyya;

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى﴾ — and in one reading with the assimilation of the tanwīn into the lām, giving it ḍamma, and without hamza — they are the people of ʿĀd, and the other ones are the people of Ṣāliḥ,

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَثَمُودَا﴾ with full declension (ṣarf) as the name of the ancestor, and as a diptote for the tribe [وَثَمُودَ]; it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عَادًا; ﴿فَمَا أَبْقَى﴾ any one of them,

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ that is, before ʿĀd and Thamūd, We destroyed them; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَى﴾ than ʿĀd and Thamūd, because of Noah's long stay among them — {فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا} — and they, besides not believing in him, used to harm him and beat him;

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ﴾ which are the towns of the people of Lot, ﴿أَهْوَى﴾ He let them fall, after raising them to the sky, overturned onto the earth, by His commanding Gabriel to do that;

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿فَغَشَّاهَا﴾ of stones after that ﴿مَا غَشَّى﴾ — left vague to inspire terror; and in Hūd: {فَجَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ}.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكَ﴾ His blessings that point to His oneness and His power ﴿تَتَمَارَى﴾ do you doubt, O human being, or deny?

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ Muhammad ﴿نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى﴾ of their kind, that is, a messenger like the messengers before him, sent to you as they were sent to their peoples.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُ﴾ the Resurrection has drawn near;

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ any soul ﴿كَاشِفَةٌ﴾ that is, none reveals it and makes it manifest but He, as in His words {لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَا إِلَّا هُوَ}.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿أَفَمِنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ that is, the Quran, ﴿تَعْجَبُونَ﴾ in denial,

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَتَضْحَكُونَ﴾ in mockery, ﴿وَلَا تَبْكُونَ﴾ on hearing its promise and its threat,

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ سَامِدُونَ﴾ amusing yourselves, heedless of what is required of you?

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ who created you ﴿وَاعْبُدُوا﴾ and do not prostrate to the idols nor worship them.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَالنَّجْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb for future time, stripped of the conditional sense. ﴿هَوى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما غَوى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ما ضل.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَما يَنْطِقُ﴾ mā is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَنِ الْهَوى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿وَحْيٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is an adjective of وحي.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿عَلَّمَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿شَدِيدُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْقُوى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is a second adjective of وحي.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿ذُو﴾ an adjective of شديد. ﴿مِرَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَاسْتَوى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِالْأُفُقِ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْأَعْلى﴾ an adjective of الأفق; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ دَنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَتَدَلَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَكانَ﴾ kāna, and its noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿قابَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿قَوْسَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it by the fāʾ. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَدْنى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قاب.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فَأَوْحى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلى عَبْدِهِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوحى; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it by the fāʾ. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَوْحى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿ما كَذَبَ﴾ mā is negating, and a past verb. ﴿الْفُؤادُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَأى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿أَفَتُمارُونَهُ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَرى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿رَآهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿نَزْلَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أُخْرى﴾ an adjective of نزلة.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿سِدْرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمُنْتَهى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿عِنْدَها﴾ an adverb of place, an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿جَنَّةُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْمَأْوى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb in the sense of حين ("when"). ﴿يَغْشَى﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿السِّدْرَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ما﴾ the fāʿil (agent) of يغشى. ﴿يَغْشَى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿زاغَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْبَصَرُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ a conjunction, and mā is negating. ﴿طَغى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿رَأى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ آياتِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾ an adjective of آيات.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿اللَّاتَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object). ﴿وَالْعُزَّى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اللات; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وَمَناةَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to العزى. ﴿الثَّالِثَةَ﴾ an adjective of مناة. ﴿الْأُخْرى﴾ an adjective of العزى. [Translator's note: so in the source; in the verse الأخرى follows مناة الثالثة and is normally parsed as a second adjective of مناة.]

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أَلَكُمُ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and لكم is an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الذَّكَرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿الْأُنْثى﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِذاً﴾ a particle of answer and requital (jawāb wa-jazāʾ). ﴿قِسْمَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿ضِيزى﴾ an adjective of قسمة; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ a particle of negation. ﴿هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْماءٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and أسماء is the khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿سَمَّيْتُمُوها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is an adjective of أسماء. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil. ﴿وَآباؤُكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ سُلْطانٍ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) min, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating. ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿الظَّنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to الظن. ﴿تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْهُدى﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ in the sense of bal. ﴿لِلْإِنْسانِ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿ما﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause has no grammatical position. ﴿تَمَنَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and لله is an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْآخِرَةُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالْأُولى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الآخرة; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and kam is predicative (khabariyya), a mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿مِنْ﴾ a preposition, and redundant (zāʾid). ﴿مَلَكٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, tamyīz (specification). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ an adjective of ملك. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of kam, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَرْضى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يشاء.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun; and ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَيُسَمُّونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إن الذين.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثى﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), annexed to الأنثى.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿وَما لَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), mā is negating, and لهم is an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) علم; and ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) min, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating. ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الظَّنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, inna is a particle resembling the verb, and الظن is its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ a nominative imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position; and عمن: the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿تَوَلَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِنا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَمْ يُرِدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿ذلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن.. is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿بِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿ضَلَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿بِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿اهْتَدى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila of man, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, لله is an advanced khabar (predicate), and mā is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position, and في السموات is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an concealed after the lām of causation, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what is indicated by the meaning of ownership in His words: وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ ... ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَساؤُا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to يجزي. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿وَيَجْزِيَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَحْسَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿بِالْحُسْنَى﴾ the two are attached to يجزي.

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الْإِثْمِ﴾ الذين is a badal (substitute) from the preceding one; and a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and كبائر is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to الإثم. ﴿وَالْفَواحِشَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿اللَّمَمَ﴾ accusative (manṣūb) as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ واسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate), and المغفرة is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾ its khabar. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time. ﴿أَنْشَأَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ conjoined to the preceding one. ﴿أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿فِي بُطُونِ﴾ an adjective of أجنة. ﴿أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَلا تُزَكُّوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ its mafʿūl; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is explanatory of cause. ﴿بِمَنِ﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿اتَّقى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila of man.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَوَلَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وَأَعْطى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تولى. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَكْدى﴾ conjoined to أعطى.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أَعِنْدَهُ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿عِلْمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of رأيت. ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هو is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَرى﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal; and ﴿لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي صُحُفِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿وَإِبْراهِيمَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to موسى. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ the relative noun, an adjective. ﴿وَفَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿أَلَّا﴾ an lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), whose noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and lā is negating. ﴿تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وِزْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أُخْرى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is a badal (substitute) from mā, so it is in the position of the genitive.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the lightened an. ﴿لَيْسَ لِلْإِنْسانِ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and للإنسان is an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾ maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya). ﴿سَعى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from mā and the verb is in the position of the nominative as the noun of laysa.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿سَوْفَ﴾ a particle of futurity. ﴿يُرى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُجْزاهُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is its second mafʿūl (object). ﴿الْجَزاءَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿الْأَوْفى﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ its advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْمُنْتَهى﴾ its postponed noun; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَضْحَكَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هو, and the clause هو أضحك is the khabar of anna. ﴿وَأَبْكى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أضحك.

daas-irab:44-44.t: Conjoined to the previous verse, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الذَّكَرَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿وَالْأُنْثى﴾ conjoined.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle not governing the jussive. ﴿تُمْنى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿النَّشْأَةَ﴾ the postponed noun of anna. ﴿الْأُخْرى﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:48-48.t: The i'rab of its like has preceded.

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ رَبُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الشِّعْرى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the khabar of anna, and the clause أنه is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عاداً﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنه, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عاد. ﴿فَما أَبْقى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, mā is negating, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is conjoined to أهلك.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وَقَوْمَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ثمود. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a verb whose implied form is "أهلك". ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا﴾ inna and its noun, and kāna and its noun, and هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿أَظْلَمَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause كانوا.. is the khabar of inna, and the clause إنهم.. is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿وَأَطْغى﴾ conjoined to أظلم.

daas-irab:53-53.t: ﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ﴾ an advanced mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَهْوى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿فَغَشَّاها﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ its second mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿غَشَّى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā.

daas-irab:55-55.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and بأي: the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تتمارى. ﴿آلاءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَتَمارى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition.

daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿هذا نَذِيرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنَ النُّذُرِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نذير. ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective of النذر.

daas-irab:57-57.t: ﴿أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَها﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كاشفة. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كاشِفَةٌ﴾ the noun of laysa; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:59-59.t: ﴿أَفَمِنْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is a particle of resumption. ﴿من هذَا﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعجبون. ﴿الْحَدِيثِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. ﴿تَعْجَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلا تَبْكُونَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:61-61.t: ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ سامِدُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿فَاسْجُدُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَاعْبُدُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اسجدوا.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَٱلنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ﴾.
He, Blessed and Exalted, swore by the Quran, because it used to come down in instalments (nujūm), a verse or two verses at a time, and between the first of its revelation and the last of it there were twenty years.
[58/ا] Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, tracing it back to ʿAbd Allāh, concerning His saying "فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوقِعِ النُّجُوم": he said: it is the muḥkam (firmly established) part of the Quran.
He said: Muḥammad told us: Abū Zakariyyā means: that which was not abrogated.
And His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿إِذَا هَوَىٰ﴾.
When it came down. It has also been mentioned that it is a star when it sets.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَىٰ﴾.
It is the answer (jawāb) to His saying: ﴿وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى﴾.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ﴾.
He is saying: he does not say this Quran from his own opinion; it is only revelation. That is because Quraysh said: he only says the Quran of his own accord; so the refutation of them came down.

farraa:5-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلْقُوَىٰ﴾.
He meant Gabriel, may Allah bless him. ﴿ذُو مِرَّةٍ﴾ is part of the naʿt (description) of «شديد القوى».
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَٱسْتَوَىٰ﴾: he and Gabriel were level at the highest horizon when he was taken on the Night Journey, and that is the highest rising-place of the sun. So He implied the noun (as a pronoun) in «استوى» and conjoined «هو» to it. Most of the speech of the Arabs is to say «استوى هُوَ وأبوه» (he and his father were level), and they hardly say «استوى وأبوه»; yet that is permissible, because there is an implied (pronoun) in the verb. One of them recited to me:
ألم تَر أن النّبْعَ يُخلقُ عُودُه * وَلا يستوى والخِرْوَعُ المتَقصِّفُ
(Do you not see that the nabʿ tree's wood grows old, yet it is not equal to the brittle castor plant?) [58/ب]
And Allah, Blessed and Exalted — and He is truest in speech — said: ﴿أئِذَا كُنَّا تُرَاباً وَأباؤنا﴾, conjoining «الآباء» to the implied (pronoun) in «كنا»; but it is good here because «تراباً» comes between them. The (full) expression is: «أئذا كنَّا تُراباً نحنُ وآباؤنا».

farraa:8-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ دَنَا﴾.
He means: Gabriel, may Allah bless him, drew near to Muhammad ﷺ until he was at the distance of two Arab bows' length or nearer. ﴿فَأَوْحَىٰ﴾: he means Gabriel, peace be upon him; ﴿إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ﴾: to Muhammad ﷺ, the servant of Allah; ﴿مَآ أَوْحَىٰ﴾.
And His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَتَدَلَّىٰ﴾: it is as though the meaning were «then he came down and drew near», but it is permissible: when the meaning of two verbs is one, or nearly one, you may put whichever of them you wish first, and say: «قد دنا فقرُبَ» (he drew near and came close) and «قرُبَ فدَنا», and «شتمنى فأساء» (he insulted me and did wrong) and «أساء فشتَمَنِى», and «قال الباطِلَ» (he spoke falsehood), because insulting and doing wrong are one thing.
Likewise His saying: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعةُ وانْشَقَّ القمر﴾.
The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: the moon was split and the Hour drew near; and the meaning is one.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مَا كَذَبَ ٱلْفُؤَادُ﴾.
The heart of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿مَا رَأَىٰ﴾: He is saying: his heart was truthful about what he saw. «كذَّبَ» is read with shadda and without it. ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, and Shayba and Nāfiʿ, the two Medinans, read it without shadda [59/ا], and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it with shadda.
It is as though whoever said «كَذْبَ» means: the heart did not belie what he saw, but rather took it as true and truthful; and it may be that he means: what he saw did not belie its owner. And whoever reads it without shadda says: (the heart) did not lie about what he saw, but was truthful about it.
«[Translator's note: «كَذْبَ» here appears in the source as printed; from the context it stands for the shadda reading «كذَّب».]»

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾.
That is: will you then deny him?
Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "أَفَتَمروْنَه" means: will you deny him?; "أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ" means: will you dispute with him? [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: ... told me] Hushaym told us, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read it: "أَفَتَمرُونَهُ".
Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Abjar, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, that he read: "أفَتَمرُونَه"; and from Shurayḥ that he read: "أفَتُمَارُونَه". That is the reading of the generality, of the people of Medina, of ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and of al-Ḥasan.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾.
He is saying: another time.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, who said: Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh was asked, while I was listening, (whether it is) «عندها جَنةُ المأوى» or «جَنَةُ المأوى», and he said: a garden among the gardens.
Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: one of the elders told me [59/ب], from al-ʿArzamī, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: a garden among the gardens.
He said: al-Farrāʾ said: it has been mentioned from some of them: ﴿جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾, meaning «أجَنَّه» (enshrouded him); this is an anomalous reading (shādhdha). And it is the garden in which the souls of the martyrs are.
«[Translator's note: the variant is printed in the source in the same form as the Quranic text; the anomalous reading meant is presumably the verbal «جَنَّهُ المأوى» (the Refuge enshrouded him).]»

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿مَا زَاغَ ٱلْبَصَرُ﴾.
The sight of Muhammad ﷺ did not swerve, with his heart, to the right or left; nor did it transgress or go beyond what it saw.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ ٱللاَّتَ وَٱلْعُزَّىٰ﴾.
The people read it with a light (unstressed) tāʾ, in the wording of His saying ﴿وَلاَتَ حِينَ مَنَاص﴾ and on the pattern of «شاة». Al-Kisāʾī used to pause on it with hāʾ: ﴿أفَرَأَيْتُمُ الّلأهْ﴾.
[185/ب] He said: al-Farrāʾ said: and I pause on the tāʾ.
[Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us:] He said: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn told me, from al-Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from Mujāhid, who said: he was a man who used to mix (yaluttu) barley-meal (sawīq) for them; and he read it «الَّلاتَّ والعُزى», doubling the tāʾ.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: a man among the merchants used to mix barley-meal for them beside al-Lāt — that is, the idol — and sell it; so it was named after that man. It was an idol belonging to Thaqīf; and al-ʿUzzā was an acacia tree (samura) belonging to Ghaṭafān, which they used to worship.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنَاةَ ٱلثَّالِثَةَ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ﴾.
Manāt was a rock belonging to Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa, which they used to worship.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-ʿUzzā to cut it down. He said: so he did it, saying:
يا عُزَّ كفرانَك لا سُبْحانَك * إنِّى رأيتُ اللهَ قد أهَانك
(O ʿUzzā, I disbelieve in you, I do not glorify you; I have seen that Allah has humiliated you.)

farraa:21-22.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَكُمُ ٱلذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ﴾.
Because they said: these idols and the angels are the daughters of Allah. So He said: ﴿أَلَكُمُ ٱلذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ تِلْكَ إِذاً قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ﴾: unjust.
All the readers read «ضِيزى» without hamza. Among the Arabs there are some who say «قِسْمَة ضَيْزَى», and some of them say «قِسْمة ضَأزَى» and «ضُؤزَى» with hamza, but no one we know of has read it so. «ضِيزَى» is on the pattern «فُعْلَى».
Even if you see its first letter with a kasra, it is like their saying «بيضٌ» (white, pl.) and «عِينٌ» (wide-eyed, pl.): their first letter was originally with a ḍamma, but they disliked leaving it with its ḍamma, so that one would say «بُوضٌ» and «عُونٌ».
The singular is «بَيضاءُ» and «عَيناءُ»; so they gave the first letter a kasra so that it would be with yāʾ, and the plural, the dual and the singular would agree.
Likewise they disliked saying «ضُوزَى», so that it would become a wāw, whereas it is from yāʾ (root). I have only judged that its first letter is (originally) with ḍamma because adjectives (nuʿūt) for the feminine come either with a fatḥa or with a ḍamma: with fatḥa, «سَكْرى» (drunk), «عَطْشَى» (thirsty); with ḍamma, «الأُنثى» (the female) and «الحُبْلى» (the pregnant). But when it is a noun that is not an adjective, its first letter takes a kasra, as in His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّر فإِنَّ الذِّكرى﴾; «الذِّكرى» is a noun for that, so it takes a kasra and is not an adjective. Likewise (الشِّعْرَى) takes a kasra on its first letter because it is a noun, not an adjective.
Al-Kisāʾī reported from ʿĪsā: «ضِيزَى».
«[Translator's note: the source prints «الحُبُلْى»; the usual form is «الحُبْلى».]»

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ لِلإِنسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّىٰ﴾: what he desires.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ ٱلآخِرَةُ وٱلأُولَىٰ﴾: the reward of both.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَمْ مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ...﴾; then He said: ﴿لاَ تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً﴾.
He used the plural, though He mentioned only one angel. That is because (كَمْ) indicates that He meant a plural; and the Arabs take «أحد» and «الواحد» in the sense of a plural. They say: «هَلْ اختصمَ أحدٌ اليومَ» (Did anyone quarrel today?), and quarrelling only takes place between two or more.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿لاَ نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾, and «بين» only applies to two or more.
And His saying: ﴿فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجزين﴾ is among what shows that «أحد» can be for the plural and for the singular.
And [the meaning of] His saying ﴿وَكَمْ مِّن مَّلَكٍ﴾ is:
of those whom you worship and claim are the daughters of Allah — their intercession will avail you nothing.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْئاً﴾.
(i.e.) against the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾ [186/ا].
He belittled them; [He is saying]: that is the measure of their minds and the extent of their knowledge, when they preferred this world to the Hereafter. And it is said: that is their extent of knowledge, that they made the angels and the idols daughters of Allah.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ﴾.
Yaḥyā and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it so, and they mentioned that it is associating partners with Allah (shirk).
«[Translator's note: the source names these readers but does not state the variant they read; the text appears to be defective here.]»
And His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ﴾.
He is saying: except what comes close, among the small sins. I have heard the Arabs say: «ضَرَبَهُ ما لمَمَ القتل» (he beat him nearly to death); (ما) is a ṣila (connective) element; he means: he beat him with a beating that came close to killing. And I heard from another: «ألَمَّ يفْعَلُ» in the sense of «كادَ يفَعلُ» (he almost did).
Al-Kalbī mentioned, with his chain of transmission, that it is the glance without deliberate intent: that is «لمم», and it is forgiven; but if he repeats the look, it is not «لمم»; it is a sin. And His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنشَأَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
He means: He produced your father Adam from the earth.
And His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: He knows you best, first and last; so do not claim purity for yourselves. Let none of you say: I did such-and-such, or I performed such-and-such. He knows best who is God-fearing.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَكْدَىٰ﴾.
That is: he gave a little, then held back from spending.

farraa:35-37.t:
﴿أَعِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَىٰ﴾ his state in the Hereafter. Then He said: ﴿أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ﴾; the meaning is: «ألم» (has he not).
﴿وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلَّذِي وَفَّىٰ﴾: he conveyed that no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another — a bearer of burdens does not carry the sin of another.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ﴾.
The people's reading is (وأنَّ); had «إِنّ» been read with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), it would have been correct.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama ibn Qays, that he read what is in al-Najm and what is in al-Jinn as (وأنّ), with a fatḥa on «إنّ».
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, the like of that.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَىٰ﴾.
He made the people of Paradise laugh by entering Paradise, and made the people of the Fire weep by entering the Fire.
The Arabs say it in their speech when one of them is reproached for impatience and weeping; he says: «إنّ الله أضحكَ وأبكى» (Allah has made to laugh and made to weep). They take it in the sense of the doings of the people of this world.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ﴾: He made the poor content with what He enriched him with; ﴿وَأَقْنَىٰ﴾: from «القُنية» (acquired property) and «النشَب» (possessions).

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿رَبُّ ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ﴾: the star that rises after Orion (al-Jawzāʾ).

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَاداً ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (عاداً) giving the nūn a kasra; and al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn mentioned that al-Aʿmash read (عادَ لُّولى), making the nūn quiescent (jazm) and not pronouncing the hamza of (الأولى).
That is the reading of the people of Medina: they made the nūn quiescent once the lām had taken a vowel; and those who gave it a kasra did so because the structure rests on the quiescence of the lām that is with the alif in «الأولى». The Arabs say «قُمْ لآن» and «قُمِ الآن» (Stand now), and «صُمِ الاثنين» and «صُمْ لثنين» (Fast on Monday), according to what I have explained to you.
And His saying: ﴿عاداً الاولَى﴾ without [186/ب] hamza: the people of Hūd specifically; a remnant of them survived and was saved with Lot, so the companions of Hūd were called «the first ʿĀd».

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿وَثَمُودَا فَمَآ أَبْقَىٰ﴾.
I have seen it in some of the codices of ʿAbd Allāh as (وثمودَ فما أبقى), without alif. It is declined fully (with nunation) in the accusative throughout the Revelation, except His saying: ﴿وآتينا ثمودَ النَّاقةَ مُبْصِرةً﴾, for there is no alif in it, so it was left undeclined (as a diptote).

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَىٰ﴾.
He means: and He overthrew the overturned city (al-muʾtafika); for Gabriel, peace be upon him, carried the villages of the people of Lot until he raised them to the sky, then dropped them down, and Allah followed them with stones. That is His saying: ﴿فغَشّاها ما غشّى﴾, of stones.

farraa:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارَىٰ﴾.
He is saying: which of the favours of your Lord do you deny, (claiming) that they are not from Him? Likewise His saying: ﴿فتَمارَوْا بالنُّذُر﴾.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا نَذِيرٌ﴾. He means: Muhammad ﷺ.
﴿مِّنَ ٱلنُّذُرِ ٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾: someone may ask: how did He say of Muhammad «من النذر الأولى» (of the former warners), when he is the last of them? This is in speech as when you say: «this is one of the children of Adam», even if he is the last or the first of them. And it is said: this is a warner of the former warnings in the Preserved Tablet.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿أَزِفَتِ ٱلآزِفَةُ﴾: the Resurrection has drawn near.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: no revealer besides Allah knows it — that is, none knows the knowledge of it but my Lord. The feminine form of (الكاشفة) is like your saying «ما لِفلانٍ باقيةٌ», meaning: (he has no) remaining; and «العافية» (well-being) and «العاقبة» (outcome), and «ليسَ له ناهيةٌ» (he has no restraint): all of this is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun).

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ﴾: heedlessly amusing yourselves.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His words «والنجم»: sworn by (muqsam bihi), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied "I swear". «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to the omitted verb "I swear", i.e. "I swear by the star at the time of its setting, whenever that is".

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (وما ينطق عن الهوى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إن» is negative, and the clause «يوحى» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «وحي».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «علَّمه» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {وَحْيٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «ذو» is an adjective (ṣifa) of {شَدِيدُ الْقُوَى}, and the clause «فاستوى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {عَلَّمَهُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the preposition «بالأفق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the clause «هو بالأفق» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «استوى».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «دنا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «استوى».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His words «أو أدنى»: a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «قاب».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فأوحى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كان»; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The wāw is resumptive; «نزلة» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «عندها جنة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {سِدْرَةِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {رَآهُ}; «ما» is a relative, the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «لقد رأى» is the response to an implied oath, and the clause of the oath and its response is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (أفرأيتم اللات والعزى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; [the verb] takes two objects, the first being «اللات» and the second the interrogative clause {أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «إذاً» is a particle of response; «ضيزى» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: (إن هي إلا أسماء) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive. The clause «سمَّيتموها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أسماء»; «أنتم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سَمَّيْتم»; the clause «ما أنزل الله بها» is a second naʿt of «أسماء»; «سلطان» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «إن يتبعون» is resumptive, and «إن» is negative; «ما» is a relative noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الظن». The clause «ولقد جاءهم الهدى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «يتبعون», i.e. they follow conjecture and the soul's desire in a state that contradicts that, namely the coming of guidance from their Lord; and the clause «لقد جاءهم» is the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: (أم للإنسان ما تمنى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فلله الآخرة والأولى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The wāw is resumptive; «كم» is the declarative (khabariyya) one, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «مِنْ ملك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم», and the clause «لا تغني» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The preposition «في السماوات» is a naʿt of «ملك»; «شيئا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition «من بعد» is attached to «تغني»; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «وما لهم به من علم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «من» is redundant (zāʾida) and «علم» is mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from «علم». The clause «إن يتبعون» is resumptive, and the clause «وإن الظن لا يغني» is a ḥāl. The preposition «من الحق» is attached to a ḥāl from «شيئا»; «شيئا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "it does not avail a little or much".

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فأعرض» is resumptive; the clause «ولم يُرِدْ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تولَّى».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The preposition «من العلم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مبلغهم»; the clause «هو أعلم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; the preposition «بمن» is attached to «أعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «ولله ما في السماوات» is resumptive. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليجزي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what is indicated by his words «ولله ما في السماوات», i.e. "His is their dominion; He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, in order to recompense the doer of good and the doer of evil". His words «بما»: the bāʾ is a preposition and «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive maṣdar is attached to «يجزي».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «الذين» is a badal (substitute) from the earlier {الَّذِينَ}; «اللمم» is excepted with a disconnected exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), accusative (manṣūb). The clause «هو أعلم» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم», and the second «إذ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first; the preposition «في بطون» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أجنَّة». The clause «فلا تزكوا» is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, i.e. "if this is your state, then do not claim purity", and the clause «هو أعلم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «قليلا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the second object of «أرأيت», and the clause «فهو يرى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause (عنده علم).

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: (أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one; the preposition «في صحف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «وإبراهيم» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to {مُوسَى}; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «أن» is lightened from the heavy form, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «تزر» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The wāw is conjunctive; «أن» is lightened, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the noun (ism) of «ليس»; the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and what follows it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the previous maṣdar, and the clause «ليس للإنسان» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن سعيه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the previous maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «يجزاه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and «الجزاء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: (وأن إلى ربك المنتهى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The maṣdar (verbal noun) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the previous maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «هو أضحك» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition «من نطفة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {خَلَقَ}; «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to the implied apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "when it is emitted, He created the two mates".

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: (وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The maṣdar (verbal noun) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the previous maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «هو أغنى» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «هو رب» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: His words «وثمود»: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to {عَادًا}. «ثمود» cannot be an object placed first, because the negative «ما» has the right to stand first in its clause (ṣadāra), so what follows it does not govern what precedes it. The clause «فما أبقى» is conjoined to {أَهْلَكَ}, and the object of «أبقى» is omitted, i.e. "anyone".

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَهْلَكَ}; the clause «إنهم كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قوم نوح», and «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The wāw is conjunctive; «المؤتفكة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed before «أهوى», and the clause «أهوى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أَهْلَكَ} in verse (50).

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «فغشَّاها» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أَهْوَى}; «ما» is a relative noun, a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the doubling in the verb is for transitivity.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «تتمارى» is resumptive; the preposition «فبأي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تتمارى».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The preposition «من النذر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نذير», and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: (أزفت الآزفة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: (ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الآزِفَةُ}; the preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from «كاشفة»; «كاشفة» is originally an adjective of an omitted feminine noun, i.e. "a removing state".

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The preposition «من هذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تعجبون», and the clause «تعجبون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: (وأنتم سامدون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in {تَعْجَبُونَ}.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, وَهُوَ بالأفق الْأَعْلَى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in استوى, i.e. "he rose, being high", meaning Gabriel, upon him be peace; so the two pronouns are for Gabriel.
Al-Farrāʾ said it [هو] is conjoined to the pronoun in استوى: he made the pronoun in استوى refer to Muhammad ﷺ and هو the pronoun of Gabriel, upon him be peace, conjoining to the nominative latent pronoun without its being emphasised, and that is ugly according to the Basrans. Had the verse been taken in this sense, the regular form according to them would be to say فاستوى هو وهو ("so he rose, he and he") at the horizon. استوى applies to one, and most often it applies to two; for that reason al-Farrāʾ made the two pronouns refer to two persons.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying أَو أدنى: أو is in its basic sense, and the meaning is: had one of you seen him, he would have said: he is the length of two bows or nearer, in closeness.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying مَا كذب الْفُؤَاد مَا رأى: whoever reads كَذَبَ without doubling makes ما in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition (accusative by removal of the preposition), i.e. "in what it saw" (فيما رأى), with ما meaning الذي, and رأى falling upon an omitted هاء, i.e. رآه; and رأى is from seeing with the eye. It is also possible that ما with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so there is no need to imply a هاء. Whoever reads كذّب with doubling makes ما a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on either of the two interpretations, and the omission of a preposition is not assumed in it, because when the verb is doubled it becomes transitive without a particle.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying نزلة أُخْرَى: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if He said "and he certainly saw him descending another descent" (ولقد رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى). According to al-Farrāʾ it is accusative because it is in the position of an adverb, since its meaning is "another time" (مرة أخرى). And the هاء in رآه refers back to Gabriel, upon him be peace.
His saying وما لهم بِهِ من علم: the هاء refers back to الأسماء (the names), because التسمية (naming) and الأسماء have the same meaning.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying وَكم من ملك: كم is the khabariyya (declarative) [كم], and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لا تغني is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying هُوَ أعلم بِمن ضل: أعلم means عالم (knowing); like it is وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى. There is room for reservation in this, because أفعل only has the meaning of فاعل when it is used by one speaking about himself. It is also possible that both are in their basic sense of preference in knowledge, i.e. He knows these two kinds, and others, better than anyone. Like that is هو أعلم بكم and هو أعلم بمن اتقى.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying ليجزي الَّذين: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning, because the meaning of ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض is "He is the Owner of all; He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, in order to recompense". It is also said that the lām is attached to His saying لا تغني شفاعتهم.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying الَّذين يجتنبون: الذين is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of الذين in His saying ويجزي الذين أحسنوا.
His saying إِلَّا اللمم: an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception), and it [اللمم] is the minor sins, from their saying ألممت بالشيء إلماما ("I touched upon the thing") when you take little of it, and زرت لماما, i.e. "I visited rarely". This is the best of the views about it.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying أَلا تزر: أن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of ما in His saying لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى, or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is: that no bearer bears" (ذلك ألا تزر). The هاء is omitted with أن, i.e. "that it is that no bearer bears" (أنه لا تزر).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying وَأَن لَيْسَ للإنسان and وَأَن سَعْيه: أن in both places is conjoined to ألا تزر. Al-Zajjāj permitted سوف يَرى with a fatḥa on the yāʾ on the assumption of an implied هاء, i.e. "he will see it" (سوف يراه); the Kufans did not permit it, because سعيه would then be governed by both أن and يرى. It is permissible according to al-Mubarrad and others, because the entry of أن upon سعيه and its governing it indicate the هاء omitted from يرى. On this basis the Basrans permitted إن زيدا ضربت ("Zayd, I struck") without a هاء.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying ثمَّ يجزاه: the هاء refers back to السعي, i.e. he will be recompensed for it; and الجزاء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying وَأَن إِلَى رَبك, وَأَنه هُوَ أضْحك, وَأَنه هُوَ أمات, وَأَنه خلق: أن in all of that is conjoined to ألا تزر on one of its two interpretations, and likewise أن in what comes after that.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t:
His saying عادا الأولى: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr assimilated the tanwīn into the lām of الأولى, after transferring the vowel of the ḍamma-vowelled hamza of أولى onto the lām of definition. Al-Mubarrad and others rejected that, because the two of them assimilated a quiescent letter into one whose origin is quiescence and whose vowel is accidental, and the accidental is not taken into account.
The justification of their reading with assimilation is what al-Māzinī and others related of the speech of the Arabs: لَحْمَر جاء ("the red one came"), meaning الأحمر; they took the vowel of the lām into account, began with it, and dispensed through it with the connective alif (alif al-waṣl). Likewise whoever assimilates the tanwīn of عاد into the lām of الأولى takes into account the vowel on the lām. On that basis they said سَلْ زيدا, which is really اسأل: when the vowel of the hamza was transferred onto the سين, it was taken into account and the connective alif was omitted. On that basis they said رُدَّ, عَضَّ and مُدَّ, whose origin is افْعَل; then the vowel of the second radical (ʿayn) was transferred onto the first radical (fāʾ), and they took it into account and omitted the connective alif because they took into account the vowel of the fāʾ, even though it was accidental.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying والمؤتفكة: accusative by أهوى.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والنجم إذا هوى﴾: the wāw is the wāw of oath; النجم is the thing sworn by, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم (I swear); إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time, stripped of the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied verb, i.e. I swear by the star at the time of its falling, so the adverb is borrowed for the ḥāl (circumstantial); the oath clause has no grammatical position because it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya); هوى is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو (it); and the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى﴾: the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; ضل صاحبكم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ما غوى is conjoined to ما ضل.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وما ينطق عن الهوى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; ينطق is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is هو (he); وعن الهوى is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينطق﴾, so عن is for passing beyond (al-mujāwaza), in its basic sense; and it has been said: it has the meaning of the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إن هو إلا وحي يوحى﴾: إن is negating; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); وحي is the khabar (predicate) of هو; and the clause يوحى is a naʿt (adjective) of وحي.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿علمه شديد القوى﴾: the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وحي﴾; علمه is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and شديد القوى is the fāʿil (agent) of علمه.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿ذو مرة فاستوى﴾: ذو مرة is a naʿt (adjective) of شديد القوى; the fāʾ is conjunctive; and استوى is a verb and an implied (muqaddar) fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وهو بالأفق الأعلى﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); وبالأفق is the khabar (predicate); الأعلى is a naʿt (adjective) of الأفق; and the clause stands in the place of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثم دنا فتدلى﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay (al-tarākhī); دنا is a verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is implied (muqaddar), its implied form being هو (he). فتدلى is conjoined to دنا.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فكان قاب قوسين أو أدنى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, with its latent (mustatir) noun; قاب قوسين is its khabar (predicate); أو is a conjunction, or is for answering (al-ijāba) [Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps «للإباحة» (for permission) or a similar term was intended]; and أدنى is conjoined to قاب.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فأوحى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿أوحى﴾ is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: ﴿هو﴾ (He), referring back to Allah the Exalted; the clause ﴿أوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿كان﴾.
﴿إلى عبده﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوحى﴾.
﴿ما﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is relative, in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or it is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and together with what it enters upon it is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, or as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿أوحى﴾: a past verb, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being: ﴿هو﴾ (he), referring back to Jibrīl, peace be upon him; the clause ﴿أوحى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى﴾: ما is negating; كذب الفؤاد is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ما is relative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because كذب is a verb that is transitive to an object; it has been said: it is not transitive, so the accusative of ما is by removal of the preposition (bi-isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), i.e.: in what he saw; and it has been said that كذب may be transitive to two objects. Or ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and together with what it enters upon it is in the position of the accusative, because it is the object of كذب.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿أفتمارونه﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); تمارونه: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿تمارونه﴾ is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: do you deny what he says and so dispute with him?
﴿على﴾: a preposition, indeclinable (mabnī).
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تمارونه﴾.
﴿يرى﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). The clause ﴿يرى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), construed together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by ﴿على﴾; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تمارونه﴾; and the clause ﴿يرى﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdar-forming ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (of the ḥāl); the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq).
﴿رآه﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿نزلة﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) of time, i.e.: another time, because the maṣdar (verbal noun) نزلة is equivalent to a single occurrence (marra) of it; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) that has taken the accusative of a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl, i.e.: he saw him descending another descent; or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar, i.e.: the seeing of another descent.
﴿أخرى﴾: a naʿt of ﴿نزلة﴾, accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿عند سدرة المنتهى﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رآه﴾, or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), or from the object, or from both together; سدرة is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and المنتهى is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿عندها جنة المأوى﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); جنة المأوى is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from سدرة المنتهى.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿إذ يغشى السدرة ما يغشى﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رآه﴾; the clause ﴿يغشى السدرة﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; ﴿السدرة﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); and the second clause ﴿يغشى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ما زاغ البصر وما طغى﴾: ما is negating; زاغ البصر is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ما طغى is conjoined to ما زاغ.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿لقد رأى من آيات ربه الكبرى﴾: the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); رأى is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); من آيات ربه is a ḥāl (circumstantial) placed before the object; and الكبرى is the object of رأى; or ﴿الكبرى﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آيات ربه﴾, and the thing seen is omitted.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أفرأيتم اللات والعزى﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ is a conjunction ordering the seeing; رأيتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and اللات is its object; and العزى is conjoined to اللات.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿ومناة الثالثة الأخرى﴾: مناة is conjoined to اللات; الثالثة الأخرى are two naʿts (adjectives): the first is a naʿt in relation to the two before it, and the second is a naʿt of disparagement for the third. The second object is omitted, its implied form being: how impotent is it? The clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: have you known the greatness and power of Allah, and then seen al-Lāt … how impotent it is?

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى﴾: the hamza is likewise for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); ولكم is a fronted khabar (predicate); الذكر is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and وله الأنثى is conjoined, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى﴾: تلك is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ (subject); إذًا has the meaning of answer and requital; قسمة is the khabar (predicate); ضيزى is a naʿt (adjective) of قسمة; and the clause is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
