﴿إن هي إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان﴾: إن is negating; هي is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); أسماء is the khabar (predicate) of هي; سميتموها is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the first being omitted, its implied form being: أصنامًا (idols); أنتم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil so that conjoining ﴿وآباؤكم﴾ to it is sound; the clause سميتموها is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أسماء﴾, and likewise the clause ما أنزل; ما is negating; أنزل الله is a verb and its fāʿil; بها is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt of ﴿سلطان﴾; من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and سلطان is genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿إن يتبعون إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس﴾: إن is negating; يتبعون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; الظن is the object of يتبعون; the wāw is a conjunction; and ما is a relative conjoined to الظن, and you may make it maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or parenthetical; the lām: the answer to the omitted oath; and قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq). جاءهم: a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ومن ربهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاءهم﴾. والهدى: the fāʿil of جاءهم. The clause ﴿ولقد جاءهم...﴾ is either a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يتبعون, or parenthetical with no grammatical position, because His words ﴿أم للإنسان...﴾ are connected to His words ﴿وما تهوى الأنفس﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿أم للإنسان ما تمنى﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the hamza of the interrogative of disapproval; ﴿للإنسان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿ما﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ﴿تمنى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿فلله الآخرة والأولى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to something implied, understood from the meaning of أم, i.e.: the matter is not so; ولله is a fronted khabar (predicate); الآخرة is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and الأولى is conjoined to الآخرة.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿وكم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and كم is the declarative (khabariyya) kam, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿من ملك﴾: in the position of the accusative as the tamyīz (specification) of the declarative kam.
﴿في السماوات﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ملك.
﴿لا﴾: لا is negating.
﴿تغني﴾: an imperfect verb.
﴿شفاعتهم﴾: a fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿لا تغني شفاعتهم﴾ is the khabar (predicate).
﴿شيئًا﴾: the object of تغني, or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. something of avail.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿من بعد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تغني﴾.
﴿أن يأذن الله﴾: أن with what falls in its scope is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive by annexation to بعد; and الله: the Name of Majesty, the fāʿil of ﴿يأذن﴾.
﴿لمن﴾: the lām is a preposition, and ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive.
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿ويرضى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿يرضى﴾ is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذين is its noun; the clause ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. وبالآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمنون﴾.
﴿ليسمون الملائكة﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); يسمون الملائكة is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿تسمية﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿الأنثى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وما لهم به من علم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما is negating; ولهم is a fronted khabar (predicate); من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; علم is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إن يتبعون إلا الظن﴾: إن is negating; يتبعون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and الظن is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وإن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (of the ḥāl); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الظن is its noun; the clause لا يغني is its khabar; ومن الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغني﴾; and شيئًا is a mafʿūl bihi, or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿فأعرض عن من تولى عن ذكرنا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); أعرض is an imperative verb; وعمن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعرض﴾; the clause ﴿تولى عن ذكرنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position. وعن ذكرنا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تولى﴾.
﴿ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لم is a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; يرد is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); الحياة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and الدنيا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿ذلك مبلغهم من العلم﴾: ذلك: a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ (subject). مبلغهم: the khabar (predicate). ومن العلم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مبلغهم﴾. The clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); رب is its noun, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); هو is a mubtadaʾ; أعلم is the khabar; وبمن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; the clause ﴿ضل عن سبيله﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause هو أعلم is the khabar of inna, and the clause ﴿هو أعلم بمن اهتدى﴾ is conjoined to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ولله: the lām is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ما is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); وفي السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿ما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾, and the clause ﴿ولله ما...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم﴾: الذين is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from الذين, or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implicit (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they are those who avoid; the clause ﴿يجتنبون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. وكبائر: the object of يجتنبون. والإثم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). والفواحش: conjoined to ﴿كبائر﴾. وإلا: a particle of exception; and اللمم: the excepted (mustathnā) by إلا, and it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and it has been said: it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil).
﴿إن ربك واسع المغفرة﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); رب is its noun, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; واسع المغفرة is its khabar; and the clause gives the reason for excepting al-lamam (minor faults), with no grammatical position.
﴿هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم﴾: هو is a mubtadaʾ; أعلم is the khabar; وبكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلم﴾; ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, also attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; the clause ﴿أنشأكم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; ومن الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنشأكم﴾; ﴿وإذ﴾ is conjoined to the first إذ; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, and أجنة is its khabar; the clause ﴿أنتم أجنة﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and ﴿في بطون أمهاتكم﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of أجنة.
﴿فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); لا is the prohibitive lā; تزكوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أنفسكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); هو is a mubtadaʾ; أعلم is the khabar; وبمن اتقى is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; and the clause اتقى is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿أفرأيت الذي تولى﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī); the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to an omitted, implied clause; رأيت is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), with the meaning of: tell me; الذي is the first object of رأيت; the clause تولى is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿أفرأيت...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وأعطى قليلا وأكدى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أعطى is conjoined to تولى; قليلًا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and you may make it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أكدى is conjoined to أعطى.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); عنده is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); علم الغيب is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause stands in the position of the accusative as the second object of رأيت; the fāʾ is conjunctive; هو is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يرى is its khabar; and the clause is conjoined to the clause أعنده علم الغيب, so it falls within the scope of the interrogative.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: بل ألم ينبأ؟ (rather, has he not been informed?). ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; ينبأ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هو (he); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of ﴿ينبأ﴾; ﴿في صحف﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. وموسى: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿وإبراهيم الذي وفى﴾: إبراهيم is conjoined to موسى; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause ﴿وفّى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى﴾: أن is lightened from the heavy (form), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause ﴿لا تزر...﴾ is its khabar (predicate); وازرة is the fāʿil (agent) of تزر; وزر أخرى is the object of تزر; and أن with what falls in its scope is a badal (substitute) from ﴿ما﴾ in صحف موسى, so it is in the position of the genitive; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو ألا تزر (it is that no bearer bears), so it is in the position of the nominative.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى﴾: أن is conjoined to ألا تزر, so it is lightened like it; the clause of ليس is its khabar (predicate); وللإنسان is the fronted khabar of laysa; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); سعى is a verb; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما سعى﴾ is the noun of laysa.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿وأن سعيه سوف يرى﴾: conjoined to what preceded; سعيه is the noun of anna; and the clause سوف يرى is the khabar (predicate) of anna.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى﴾: ثم is a conjunction; يجزاه is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هو (he); the hāʾ is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), or it is a second object; one says: جزيته سعيه, and: بسعيه (I requited him his striving / for his striving); الجزاء is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); الأوفى is a naʿt (adjective); the nominative pronoun refers back to man (al-insān), and the accusative one refers back to the requital [Translator's note: so in the source, «يعود على الجزاء»; given the example just cited, the striving (السعي) may be meant]; and the clause is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of anna.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وأن إلى ربك المنتهى﴾: conjoined to what preceded; وإلى ربك is the fronted khabar (predicate) of anna; and المنتهى is the postponed noun of anna.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى﴾: also conjoined; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause أضحك is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of anna; or ﴿هو﴾ is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of anna; and it has been said: it is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and the clause أضحك is the khabar of anna.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿وأنه هو أمات وأحيا﴾: conjoined to the previous ayah; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿أمات﴾ is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of anna; or ﴿هو﴾ is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of anna; and it has been said: it is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and the clause ﴿أمات﴾ is the khabar of anna.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿وأنه خلق الزوجين الذكر والأنثى﴾: conjoined to the previous ayah; the clause خلق is the khabar (predicate) of anna; الزوجين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذكر is a badal (substitute) from الزوجين; and الأنثى is conjoined to الذكر.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿من نطفة إذا تمنى﴾: من نطفة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, putting its condition in the genitive (by annexation) and made accusative by its apodosis; and the clause تمنى is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى﴾: the ayah is conjoined to what precedes it; وعليه is the fronted khabar (predicate) of anna; النشأة is its postponed noun; and الأخرى is a naʿt (adjective) of النشأة.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى﴾: conjoined to the previous ayah; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿أغنى﴾ is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of anna; or ﴿هو﴾ is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of anna; and it has been said: ﴿هو﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and the clause ﴿أغنى﴾ is the khabar of anna.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿وأنه هو رب الشعرى﴾: أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); رب is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma; الشعرى: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the implied (muqaddara) kasra; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna; and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to its preceding counterpart.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿وأنه أهلك عادا الأولى﴾: أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause أهلك is its khabar (predicate); عادًا is the object of أهلك; and الأولى is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿وثمود فما أبقى﴾: conjoined to عاد; the fāʾ is conjunctive; and ما أبقى is conjoined to أهلك. It has been said: وثمودًا is accusative by an implicit verb, i.e.: and He destroyed Thamūd; and it cannot be a fronted object of أبقى, because the negating ما has the right to the head of the clause (al-ṣadāra), so what comes after it cannot govern what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿وقوم نوح﴾: conjoined to ثمود.
﴿من قبل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial); قبل has been made indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning.
﴿إنهم كانوا هم أظلم وأطغى﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw of the plural is its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in كانوا; أظلم is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا; and أطغى is conjoined to أظلم.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿والمؤتفكة أهوى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; المؤتفكة is a fronted object of أهوى; and the clause is conjoined. Or المؤتفكة is a noun conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿فغشاها ما غشى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; غشاها is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); ما is a relative, the second object of ﴿غشى﴾; and the clause غشى is the ṣila (relative clause). Or غشّى with the doubled letter has the meaning of the bare form, so it is transitive to one object, and the fāʿil is ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربك تتمارى﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); the bāʾ is locative (ẓarfiyya); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تتمارى﴾; تتمارى is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the implied (muqaddara) ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت (you); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the power of Allah is embodied in what has been mentioned, then which of your Lord's bounties do you dispute?

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿هذا نذير من النذر الأولى﴾: the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); نذير is the khabar (predicate); ومن النذر is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نذير﴾; النذر is either the plural of the active participle, if we consider نذير an irregular active participle, or of the maṣdar (verbal noun), if we consider نذير an irregular maṣdar, because it is from أنذر, and the regular active participle from it is منذر, and the regular maṣdar from it is منذر [Translator's note: so in the source; the regular maṣdar of أنذر is إنذار]; and الأولى is a naʿt of النذر.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿أزفت الآزفة﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الآزفة; ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ولها is a fronted khabar (predicate); ومن دون الله is a ḥāl; كاشفة is the noun of laysa, and it may be an adjective (waṣf) or a maṣdar (verbal noun); if it is an adjective, the tāʾ in it is for the feminine, because it is then a naʿt (adjective) of something omitted, i.e.: a soul that removes (it), or: a state that removes (it).

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿أفمن هذا الحديث تعجبون﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ومن هذا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعجبون﴾; الحديث is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; and تعجبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿وأنتم سامدون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (of the ḥāl) or resumptive; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); سامدون is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the position of the accusative, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿فاسجدوا لله واعبدوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); اسجدوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; ولله: the lām is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اسجدوا﴾; اعبدوا is an imperative verb conjoined to ﴿فاسجدوا﴾; and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
وَالنَّجْمِ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath, and the implied form is "and by the Lord of the star". إِذا هَوى is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "when it fell". The answer to the oath is ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ, i.e. he has not swerved from the right course. وَما غَوى: it was said:
i.e. nor has he been disappointed in the mercy he sought.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: وَما يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوى: it was said: the meaning is "and he does not speak [from desire] in what he reports of the revelation"; and what indicates this is إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحى, i.e. what he reports is nothing but a revelation revealed. يوحى goes back to the yāʾ [as its final radical]; had it been among the verbs with final wāw, the imperfect would have followed the past.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: I.e. the means. Al-Farrāʾ related that it is read شَدِيدُ الْقُوى with a kasra on the qāf, because fuʿla and fiʿla resemble each other. Qatāda said: شديد القوى is Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
ذُو مِرَّةٍ: Mujāhid said: Jibrāʾīl, upon him be peace, possessor of strength. Ibn Zayd said: المرّة is strength. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ذُو مِرَّةٍ, i.e. of beautiful appearance. Abū Jaʿfar said:
the literal meaning of المرّة in the language is soundness of build and freedom from defects and infirmities; and when [a being] is like that, it is strong. فَاسْتَوى: it was said: so he stood upright, after he had been descending swiftly.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
[وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلى] is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "so he stood upright, being high". This is the view of those scholars by whom proof is established; the meaning accords with it, and the iʿrāb supports it. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning is "so Muḥammad ﷺ and Jibrīl, upon him be peace, stood upright", making «وهو» refer to Jibrāʾīl, upon him be peace, and conjoining it to the latent pronoun. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is the error of conjoining to a nominative latent pronoun that has no [overt] sign; similar to it is "مررت بزيد جالسا وعمرو" (I passed by Zayd sitting, and ʿAmr), conjoining it to the nominative latent pronoun. This is forbidden in speech unless the latent pronoun is emphasised or the speech is lengthened. Then he likened it to His saying: أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً وَآباؤُنا [al-Naml:
67]. This comparison is wrong in two respects. One of them is that the speech has been lengthened here, and the direct object stands in place of the emphasis. The other respect is that here the conjunction is to the nūn and alif, and your saying "قمنا وزيد" (we stood, and Zayd) is easier than your saying "قام وزيد" (he stood, and Zayd). Moreover, the meaning is not as he mentioned.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: Al-Farrāʾ likened it to His saying, Majestic and Mighty: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ [al-Qamar: 1], because the meaning [there] is "the moon split and the Hour drew near". Abū Jaʿfar said: This comparison is a clear error, because the rule of the fāʾ is different from the rule of the wāw, since it indicates that the second comes after the first. So the implied form is "then he drew near, and increased in nearness".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: This too is among what is problematic in Arabic, because «أو» cannot be in the sense of the wāw, owing to the difference between them, nor in the sense of «بل», for the reason we have mentioned; and conciseness requires something else. So the implied form is "and he was, by your measure, had you seen him, the measure of two bow-lengths or nearer", as is related from Ibn Masʿūd; he said: "and he was the measure of one cubit or two cubits". Abū Jaʿfar said: القاد, القيد, القاب, القيب, القدر and القدر [all mean "measure"].

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
There are two views on its meaning. Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī related from Qatāda from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said:
عبده is Muḥammad ﷺ. He interpreted this according to the meaning: "so He revealed to His servant Muḥammad ﷺ". The other view is that the meaning is "so Jibrāʾīl revealed to Muḥammad ﷺ, the servant of Allah"; it is the view of a group of the people of tafsīr, among them Ibn Zayd. He said: and this is more in keeping with the context of the speech, because what is before it and what is after it are reports about Jibrāʾīl ﷺ and Muḥammad ﷺ, so it does not depart from them to anyone else except by a proof which must be accepted.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
This is the reading of most of the readers. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read ما كَذَبَ الْفُؤادُ with a doubled [dhāl]. [Translator's note: the doubled reading is printed without the shadda in the source; it is ما كَذَّبَ.] The implied form with the light [reading] is "the heart of Muḥammad did not belie Muḥammad in what he saw"; and في was omitted, just as «من» was omitted in His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا [al-Aʿrāf: 155], because it is among the verbs that take two objects, one of them by means of a preposition. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear explanation, and we know of no grammarian who has explained it. As for the one who read كذّب, al-Farrāʾ claimed that it may mean the owner of the heart; and he permitted the meaning of «ما كذب» to be "affirmed as true". The reading with the light [form] is clearer in meaning; with the doubling it is far-fetched, because its meaning [would be] "accepted it", and when the heart has accepted it, i.e. known it, there is no sense in denial. The reading with the light [form] is clear, i.e. it told him the truth. The people of interpretation differed on the meaning of ما كَذَبَ الْفُؤادُ ما رَأى. Ibn ʿAbbās and a group with him said: he saw his Lord, Majestic and Mighty. He said: Allah singled out Ibrāhīm ﷺ with intimate friendship, Mūsā with speech, and Muḥammad ﷺ with vision, as came in the ḥadīth from him ﷺ:
«I saw my Lord, Majestic and Mighty, and He said: About what does the Highest Assembly dispute?» The other view is that of Ibn Masʿūd and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them both: that he saw Jibrāʾīl in his [true] form. Zirr traced it back from ʿAbd Allāh [to the Prophet]: the Prophet ﷺ said: «I saw Jibrāʾīl in his [true] form, having six hundred wings, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.» ʿĀʾisha also traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, and she rejected what Ibn ʿAbbās said.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
[The reading أَفَتَمْرُونَهُ] is soundly reported from the Prophet ﷺ, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. It is the reading of Masrūq, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, and al-Nakhaʿī read it so — except that Abū Ḥātim related that he said: "They did not dispute with him; rather, they denied him." He said: and in this there is a criticism of a group of readers whose reading constitutes a proof, among them al-Ḥasan, Shurayḥ, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and the two ʿĀṣims. What is to be said about this is that they are two widespread readings which the community has read, except that the first is [the one read by] those we have mentioned of the Companions. [Translator's note: the entry begins in mid-discussion; the two readings concerned are أَفَتَمْرُونَهُ and أَفَتُمارُونَهُ, which the source does not quote here.]
As for saying "they did not dispute with him", that is a grave [claim], because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has informed us that they argued, and arguing is disputation (المراء), especially in this story; they disputed with him about it, until they said to him: "You travelled in a single night to Bayt al-Maqdis; then describe it to us"; and they said: "We have a caravan in Syria; tell us news of it." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: one says "مراه بحقّه يمريه" when he denies him his right and withholds it from him. He said: and «على» is in the sense of «عن». Abū Jaʿfar said: That is well known in the language; we have mentioned that in the dialect of Banū Kaʿb ibn Rabīʿa [one says] "رضي الله عليك", i.e. "عنك" (may Allah be pleased with you).

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرى (13): the best and soundest of what has been said about it is that the pronoun refers back to شديد القوى, as al-Ḥasan ibn Ghulayb told us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Sawwār al-Kūfī told us; he said: ʿAbda ibn Sulaymān told us from Saʿīd from Abū Maʿshar from Ibrāhīm from Masrūq; he said: ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Three things — whoever says one of them has uttered a tremendous lie against Allah, Majestic and Mighty: whoever claims that he knows what will happen tomorrow has uttered a tremendous lie against Allah — وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَداً [Luqmān: 34]; whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ concealed anything of the matter of the revelation has uttered a tremendous lie against Allah, while Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says: يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ [al-Māʾida: 67]; and whoever claims that Muḥammad saw his Lord has uttered a tremendous lie against Allah, Majestic and Mighty, while Allah, exalted be His praise, says: وَما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْياً أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ حِجابٍ [al-Shūrā: 51], and Allah says: لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ [al-Anʿām: 103]." I said: "O Mother of the Believers, has He not said: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرى (13) and وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ [al-Takwīr: 23]?" She said: "I asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: «I saw Jibrāʾīl, upon him be peace, descending, filling the horizon, in his [true] build and majesty» — or "his build and form"." Al-Farrāʾ said: «نزلة أخرى» means "another time". Abū Jaʿfar said: «نزلة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say "جاء فلان مشيا" (so-and-so came walking), i.e. "on foot (ماشيا)"; the implied form is "and he saw him descending another descent", i.e. during his descent. عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهى (14) is connected with رآه. ʿIkrima said from Ibn ʿAbbās: I asked Kaʿb about the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said: To it the knowledge of the learned ends; no one knows what is beyond it except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: it was named the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary because the souls of the believers end at it. The school of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that whatever of the command of Allah comes from above it or from below it ends at it. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no view among these but that it is possible, and there is no report that settles the matter decisively; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Kaʿb said: the refuge of the souls of the martyrs. Qatāda said: the refuge of the souls of the believers. And it is said:
it is the Garden in which Ādam, upon him be peace, took refuge, and it is in the seventh heaven. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has made known, on this [view], that Muḥammad ﷺ was taken by night to the seventh heaven. As for the one who read جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوى, its implied form is "the darkness of the night covered [him]". [Translator's note: the variant is printed with the same spelling as the standard reading; it is جَنَّهُ الْمَأْوى, with a verb.] It is an anomalous reading which the Companions Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar rejected. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is like جَنَّاتُ الْمَأْوى [al-Sajda:
19] — a clear proof, together with the consensus of the community by whom proof is established. Moreover, one says "أجنّه الليل" and "جنّ عليه", while "جنّه الليل" is an anomalous dialect form.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t:
إِذْ is connected with رآه. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: the light of the Lord covered it, and the angels were alighting on the trees like crows. Abū al-ʿĀliya said the same, and it is said that something similar is from Abū Hurayra, and he added to it:
"and there his Lord, Majestic and Mighty, spoke to him [and] said to him: Ask." ما زاغَ الْبَصَرُ, i.e. it did not turn aside to the right or left in bewilderment.
وَما طَغى, i.e. nor did it go beyond that without discerning it.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: Ibn Zayd said: he saw Jibrāʾīl ﷺ in his [true] form in heaven.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: the pause on it is اللّاه; someone else said: the pause on it is اللّات. They derived it from the name of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and it is written in the copies (maṣāḥif) with tāʾ. And they derived العزّى from العزيز. وَمَناةَ is from "منى الله عزّ وجلّ عليه الشيء", i.e. He decreed it. الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرى is a naʿt (adjective) of مناة.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: It may be placed earlier while intended to come later, and the meaning would be: "Those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the naming of females", i.e. they say they are daughters of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Is the male, whom you are pleased with, for you, and the female, whom you are not pleased with, for Him?"

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: One says ضازه يضيزه and يضوزه, when he treats him unjustly.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْماءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوها أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ: their saying that the idols are gods and the angels are daughters of Allah. ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِها مِنْ سُلْطانٍ, i.e. any proof or revelation; it is only something you have fabricated. إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَما تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ, i.e. in this naming they follow nothing but conjecture and their desires. وَلَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدى, i.e. the clear statement that there is no object of worship besides Him and that worshipping these things is polytheism and disbelief.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
It was said: i.e. that is not his. Ibn Zayd said: i.e. if Muḥammad ﷺ wished for something, it is his.
The explanation of this view: if Muḥammad ﷺ wished for the messengership, Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has given it to him, so do not deny it.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: He gives whom He wills whatever He wills.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّماواتِ: had you omitted «من», you would still put [ملك] in the genitive, because it is [كم of] report (khabar), and «كم» puts what follows it in the genitive in a report, like «ربّ», except that «كم» is for many and ربّ for few. لا تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَرْضى: in this there is an alerting and a rebuke to them, because they said ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفى [al-Zumar: 3]; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, informed [them] that the angels, Allah's blessings and peace be upon them — who are the most excellent of creatures before Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the most abundant of them in acts of obedience — their intercession avails nothing except after the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His good pleasure; so how could the idols intercede for them?

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: It is their saying that they are the daughters of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ما لهم بذلك من علم: مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and the position is the position of the nominative. إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئاً, i.e. it is of no benefit in place of the truth and does not stand in its stead.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: I.e. leave whoever has turned away from Our remembrance, and has not believed nor affirmed [Allah's] oneness, and has not wanted the reward of the Hereafter, and has wanted nothing but the adornment of the life of this world.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: ذلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ: Ibn Zayd said: they have no knowledge except the polytheism and disbelief they are in, and their stubborn opposition to what has come from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Someone else said: "that is the extent of their knowledge": that they preferred the perishing adornment and leadership of this world to the lasting reward of the Hereafter. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ: أعلم may be in the sense of عالم (knowing), and it may be in its own sense [i.e. comparative] with an omission; and [سبيله is] the path of Islam. وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدى, i.e. to the way of truth, which is Islam; and that is in His prior knowledge.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: The lām of kay (purpose) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning, i.e. "and to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills". لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَساؤُا, i.e. disbelieved and disobeyed, بِما عَمِلُوا. And the lām may be attached to His saying, Majestic and Mighty: لا تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً. لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسئوُا بِما عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَى: conjoined. It was said: الحسنى is Paradise. Zayd ibn Aslam said: الَّذِينَ أَساؤُا are the disbelievers and الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا are the believers.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
الَّذِينَ is a badal (substitute) from the الذين before it. يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الْإِثْمِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it in Sūrat «Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf». وَالْفَواحِشَ is conjoined to الكبائر. إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ: we have mentioned what the people of tafsīr say about it. It is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ) not of the same kind as the first (i.e. a disjoined exception). Among the soundest and most comprehensive of the scholars' views on it is that it is the minor sins, taken from "لممت بالشيء" when you take only a little of it.
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ واسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ, i.e. for those who commit minor sins; and analogous to it is إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 31]. هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ, i.e. He knew better what you would do and what you would come to, when He began the creation of your father from dust, and when you were embryos in your mothers' wombs, than you [know it] now that you have grown up. And أعلم may be in the sense of عالم. فَلا تُزَكُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: Zayd ibn Aslam said: i.e. do not declare them free of sins. He said:
and the explanation of this is: do not say "we are pure". هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقى sins, feared [Allah] and performed the obligatory duties.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
I.e. from faith. Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning a man who became Muslim; his companion met him, reproached him and said to him: "You have declared your father astray and attributed disbelief to him, while you are more deserving of [being made] Christian [like] them." He said: "I feared the punishment of Allah." He said:
"Give me something, and I will bear the punishment for you." So he gave him a little, then became niggardly and stopped giving; and he wrote him a document and had it witnessed against himself that he would bear the punishment for him. So أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى was revealed.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: I.e. he was niggardly with him. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «أكدى» means "he withheld"; and Mujāhid said: "he cut off".

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: I.e. does he know that this one will bear the punishment for him? As He said; and يرى is in the sense of يعلم (knows); Sībawayh related it.

nahhas-irab:36-37.t: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِما فِي صُحُفِ مُوسى (36) وَإِبْراهِيمَ: that no one is punished for another. ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَإِبْراهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى — he said: before Ibrāhīm, upon him be peace, one would be seized [for another's crime]. [What follows] is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "that is: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى". The implied form according to Mujāhid: he fulfilled what was made obligatory upon him. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: he fulfilled [the command] by sacrificing his son. The most correct of what has been said about the meaning of the verse is what its generality indicates, i.e. he fulfilled everything made obligatory upon him of the laws of Islam; and وفّى in Arabic is for intensity. [Translator's note: the passage «فيؤخذ موضع رفع» appears to have lost words in the source; it has been rendered as "one would be seized [for another's crime]. [What follows] is in the position of the nominative".]

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: «أن» is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «ما», and it may be in the position of the nominative, i.e. "that is: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى". The implied form according to Sībawayh is "that (أنه) no bearer of burdens bears…". One says وزر يزر: he bore the burden.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: In the sense of "and that (وأنه)" also, i.e. a person is recompensed only for what he has done. [Translator's note: so printed, without a negative particle; the sense "is recompensed only for" requires «لا يجازى».]

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
That people will be shown on the Day of Resurrection what he did of good or evil, because he will be recompensed for it. Abū Isḥāq said: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرى (40) is permissible. He said: and this is not permissible according to the Kufans; they forbade "أنّ زيدا ضربت", and gave as the reason for that that it is an error because two governing words do not govern زيد, namely «أنّ» and «ضربت». Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and their followers, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, permitted it. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I asked Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, and said to him: "You do not permit 'زيد ضربت' and you differ with Sībawayh on it; so how have you permitted 'أنّ زيدا ضربت', when «أنّ» enters upon the mubtadaʾ (subject)?" He said: "This is different from that, because when «إنّ» has entered, you are forced to imply the hāʾ, since there are two governing words in the speech." [Translator's note: the opening of the entry and Abū Isḥāq's "permissible" form appear to concern a variant (e.g. accusative سعيَه … يُرى) whose vowelling is not shown in the source.]

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: ثُمَّ يُجْزاهُ الْجَزاءَ: [الجزاء] is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the hāʾ refers to the striving. الأوفى: because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has fulfilled for them what He promised and threatened.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: [المنتهى] is in the position of the accusative as the noun of «أنّ», except that it is a maqṣūr noun in which the iʿrāb does not appear. The meaning is: and that to your Lord is the end of all His creatures and their return, so He will recompense them for their good and evil deeds.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«هو» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and it may be a qualifier of the hāʾ. As for the meaning of أضحك and أبكى, it was said concerning it: He made the people of Paradise laugh by their entering Paradise, and made the people of the Fire weep by their entering the Fire. And it was said:
He makes whom He wills of [the people of] this world laugh by gladdening him, and makes whom He wills weep by grieving him; and the verse is general.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: I.e. He caused to die whoever died, and gave life to whoever lives, by placing the spirit in him after he had been a drop of fluid.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: Each one of them is a mate (زوج) of the other, and الذكر والأنثى is a badal (substitute) from الزوجين.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
I.e. when the man and the woman emit it (أمناها). It was said: it is from "منى الله عليه الشيء" when He decrees a thing for him.
The first is from «أمنى», and this one is from «منى»; and yufʿal (the imperfect) of the triliteral and the quadriliteral is the same [in form], because a letter is dropped from the quadriliteral: you say هو يكرم, the original being يؤكرم; the hamza was dropped to conform with your saying أنا أكرم, and it was dropped from أكرم because two hamzas do not come together.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: I.e. it is incumbent on Him to bring the two mates into being [again] after death.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: أقنى means "He made content". Ibn Zayd said: He enriched some of His creatures and impoverished others. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says "أقنيت الشيء", i.e. I took it to keep with me and made it permanent; so أقنى means "He gave him lasting wealth".

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: Mujāhid said: it is Sirius (al-Shiʿrā), which is behind al-Jawzāʾ (Orion). Someone else said: they are two Shiʿrās, and the one that has crossed over is al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr, which is outside the Milky Way, which Abū Kabsha worshipped in the Jāhiliyya; and he said: "I saw it cross over the [lunar] mansions."

nahhas-irab:50-50.t:
[عاداً الْأُولى] is the reading of the Kufans and some of the Meccans, and it is the clear reading in Arabic: the nunation was given a vowel because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Medina is «وأنه أهلك عادا الولي», with the nunation assimilated into the lām. The grammarians spoke about this. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is a solecism (laḥn). Someone else said: it cannot be other than one of two ways: either one declines عاد [as a triptote] and says عاداً الأولى, or one treats it as a diptote, making it a name for the tribe, and says عادَ الأولى. As for عادا الأولى, it is intermediate. As for the argument for the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr, we mention it from Abū Isḥāq. He said: there are three dialect forms in it: one says الأولى with the hamza pronounced; then the hamza is lightened and its vowel transferred to the lām, so you say «الولي», and the connecting alif is not dropped, because it remains with the alif of interrogation, as in آللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ [Yūnus: 59], so it differed from [other] connecting alifs and was not dropped here either. The third dialect form is to say «لولى», dropping the connecting alif, because it was only brought in because of the vowellessness of the lām, so when the lām received a vowel it was dropped. On this [basis] is his reading عادا الولي, assimilating the nunation into the lām. He said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: assimilating the nunation into this lām is not permissible, because the basic state of this lām is vowellessness and the nunation is vowelless, so it is as though two vowelless letters were combined. He said: and I heard him say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: "I do not know that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ committed a solecism in pure Arabic in anything of the Qur'an except in يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ [Āl ʿImrān:
75] and in وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عاداً الْأُولى." He said: Abū Isḥāq rejected this and argued with what we have presented. As for الأولى, it is said: there is no "first" unless there is an "other"; so was there a later ʿĀd? A group of scholars spoke about this. Among the best of what has been said about it is what Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq mentioned; he said: the first ʿĀd is ʿĀd ibn Iram ibn ʿAwḍ ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ ﷺ, and the second ʿĀd is Banū Luqaym ibn Hazzāl ibn Huzayl, of the descendants of the elder ʿĀd; they were in Mecca at the time the first ʿĀd was destroyed, along with Banū ʿImlāq. Abū Isḥāq said: they remained after the first ʿĀd until some of them transgressed against others and they killed one another. He said:
And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: the later ʿĀd is Thamūd; and he cited as evidence for that the saying of Zuhayr [in the ṭawīl metre]: 440-
كأحمر عاد ثمّ ترضع فتفطم
(Like the Red One of ʿĀd; then she suckles and weans.)
 meaning the one who hamstrung the she-camel. A third answer is that there may be a thing that has a first and no last; of that is the bliss of the people of Paradise.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: One of the scholars said: i.e. He did not leave them in their disbelief and disobedience, but annihilated them and destroyed them. This view is an error, because what comes after the fāʾ does not govern what comes before it, so it is not permissible to make ثمودا accusative by أبقى; moreover, after the fāʾ there is «ما», and most grammarians do not permit what comes after ما to govern what is before it. What is correct is that ثمودا is accusative by conjunction to عاد.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ is conjoined as well. مِنْ قَبْلُ, i.e. before these. إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغى, i.e. more unjust to themselves than these, and more transgressing, more extreme in overstepping into injustice. Qatāda made that clear; he said: a man of them would walk his son to Nūḥ, upon him be peace, and say: "My son, accept nothing from this man, for my father walked me to him and enjoined on me what I have enjoined on you." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described them with injustice and transgression.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: The benefit is that this is a meaning of magnification, i.e. "what covered [them], of what has been mentioned to you". Qatāda said: He covered it with rocks, i.e. after He had raised it and overturned it.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: I.e. say, O Muḥammad, to whoever doubts and disputes: "Which of the blessings of your Lord do you doubt (تمتري)?", i.e. تشكّ. The singular of الآلاء is إلى; and one also says ألى, إلي and أليّ — four dialect forms. Qatāda said: i.e. "which of the blessings of your Lord do you dispute about?"; the meaning is "O man, which of the blessings of your Lord do you doubt?", because المرية is doubt.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: هذا نَذِيرٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). The school of Qatāda is that the meaning is "this Muḥammad is a warner", and its explanation is that the meaning is "this Muḥammad is one of the warners", i.e. one of them in kind, truthfulness and resemblance; and when he is like them, he is one of them. The school of Abū Mālik is that the meaning is "this that I have warned you of, the destruction of the nations, is a warning" مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولى. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is more fitting to the sequence of the verse, because before it is أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِما فِي صُحُفِ مُوسى وَإِبْراهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى [verse: 3], so the implied form is "this that I have warned you of is of the earlier warnings". [Translator's note: the verse reference "3" is as printed; the quoted words are verses 36–37 of this sūra.]

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: «الآزفة» is one of the names of the Resurrection. He said: one says أزف الشيء when a thing draws near, as he said [in the kāmil metre]: 441-
أزف التّرحّل غير أنّ ركابنا ... لمّا نزل برحالنا وكأن قد
(Departure has drawn near, except that our mounts have not yet gone off with our saddles — and it is as though they had.)

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: It was said: the meaning of «كاشفة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "removal", like لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ [al-Wāqiʿa: 2]. Abū Isḥāq said: «كاشفة» means one who makes clear when it will be. It was also said: «كاشفة» means one who removes the hardship that is in it, i.e. "for its occurrence there is no remover except Allah, Mighty and Majestic", and He removes it only from the believers; and the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) is for intensification.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: I.e. are you astonished that He revealed to Muḥammad ﷺ?

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: وَتَضْحَكُونَ in mockery. وَلا [تبكون]: because of the threat and the mention of punishment in it.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: I.e. diverting yourselves, turning away from His signs.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ, and do not prostrate to al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt. وَاعْبُدُوا, i.e. and worship Allah, Majestic and Mighty, alone.

safi-cedvel:1-10.t:
* I'rab:
(والنجم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم; (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the omitted verb of the oath «[Note: There is a difficulty in this attachment: the verb of the oath is performative (inshāʾ), and the performative indicates the present, whereas the adverb (إذا) indicates the future, so there is a discrepancy between the two times ... To remove the difficulty the speech is construed as: I swear by the star at the time of its falling, whatever that time may be; the adverb on this view is borrowed for the present ...]» , (ما) negative in the three places; (عن الهوى) attached to (ينطق)..
The clause « (أقسم) بالنجم ... » has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya); the clause «هوى ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «ما ضلّ صاحبكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath; the clause «ما غوى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the oath; and the clause «ما ينطق ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the oath. 4- 7- (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr), and the third-person pronoun in (علّمه) refers back to the Messenger, upon him be peace; (شديد) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. an angel severe in power; (ذو) a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هو), (الفاء) conjunction, and the fāʿil of (استوى) refers back, according to the apparent sense, to Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: There are differing views on what the agent pronoun refers to: it was said that it refers to the Noble Quran, which settled in the breast of Jibrīl or in the breast of the Messenger, upon him be peace ... or it refers to the Messenger, i.e. he became upright in his strength or in his mission.. or it refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. He established Himself on the Throne.]» , (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (هو) mubtadaʾ, i.e. Jibrīl; (بالأفق) khabar ...
The clause «إن هو إلّا وحي ... » has no grammatical position, being causal — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) —; the clause «يوحى ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of وحي; the clause «علّمه شديد ... » is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of وحي, the link between them being implied (muqaddar), i.e. one severe in power taught it to him; the clause «استوى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause علّمه; and the clause «هو بالأفق ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of استوى «[Note: On the assumption that the agent is Jibrīl; under the other construals of the agent the clause is resumptive.]» 8- 10- (ثمّ) a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) in the two places, and the fāʿil of (دنا, تدلّى) is a pronoun referring back to Jibrīl, and likewise the noun of kāna; (قاب) the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb); (أو) a conjunction, and the fāʿil of the first (أوحى) is a pronoun referring back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, understood from the context of the verse in His saying عبده; (إلى عبده) attached to (أوحى), and the servant is Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: It was said that it is the Prophet ﷺ, and the agent of both verbs in that case is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.]» , (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil of the second (أوحى) is a pronoun referring back to عبده, i.e. what Jibrīl revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.
The clause «دنا ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause استوى; the clause «تدلّى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause دنا; the clause «كان قاب قوسين ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تدلّى; the clause «أوحى (the first) » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of His saying, the Exalted: علّمه شديد القوى; and the clause «أوحى (the second) » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(6) مرّة: a noun meaning strength, vigour, soundness of mind, firmness ... etc.; its wazn is فِعلة, with kasra on the fāʾ, on the wazn of the maṣdar of manner. (8) دنا: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its imperfect is يدنو; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. (تدلّى), it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is تدلّي — because the weak letter comes fifth, and its origin is wāw, from which is الدلو (the bucket) — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. (9) قاب: a noun meaning measure; of the bow, it is what is between the handle and its tip, and the bow has two qābs; its wazn is فعَل, with two fatḥas, and the alif in it is converted from wāw, its origin being قوب with two fatḥas; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. In the construction (قاب قوسين) there is an inversion (qalb), the origin being قابي قوس ...
(قوسين), dual of قوس, a concrete noun for the well-known instrument of war, or meaning the forearm's length; قوس is treated as masculine and feminine; its plural is قسي, its wazn فليّ with two kasras and a doubled yāʾ, and أقواس on the wazn أفعال, and قياس on the wazn فِعال with kasra on the fāʾ; it contains iʿlāl, its origin being قواس: when the qāf before the wāw took kasra, the wāw was converted to yāʾ. (10) أوحى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is أوحي — with a yāʾ at its end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Rhetoric:
The art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, فَأَوْحى إِلى عَبْدِهِ ما أَوْحى.
This is a magnification of the revelation that Allah revealed to him; the magnification is due to the vagueness in it, as though it were too great to be encompassed by any description. It is like His saying: (إِذْ يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ ما يَغْشى) and His saying (فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ).

* Benefits:
- The Night Journey (al-Isrāʾ) and the Ascension (al-Miʿrāj)..
This was before the Hijra, and it was with his body and soul together. As for al-Isrāʾ, it is his travelling by night to Bayt al-Maqdis; as for al-Miʿrāj, it is his ascent to the highest heavens. This has come in the sound hadiths.
From Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was brought al-Burāq, an animal above a donkey and below a mule, which places its hoof at the furthest extent of its sight. I mounted it until I came to Bayt al-Maqdis, and tied it to the ring; then I entered the mosque and prayed two rakʿas in it; then I came out, and Jibrīl brought me a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibrīl said:
'You have chosen the fiṭra (the natural disposition).' Then we were taken up to the first heaven, up to the seventh." Jibrīl would ask for the gate to be opened at each heaven, and it would be said to him: Who are you? He would say: Jibrīl, and with me is Muhammad ﷺ. It would be asked: Has he been sent for? Jibrīl would say: Yes. And he ﷺ met a prophet in every heaven: in the first he met Ādam, in the second Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā, in the third Yūsuf, in the fourth Idrīs, in the fifth Hārūn, in the sixth Mūsā, and in the seventh Ibrāhīm, upon them be blessing and peace. "Then he took me to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā), and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruits like large jars. When there covered it of the command of my Lord what covered it, it changed, so that none of Allah's creation is able to describe it for its beauty. Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed, and He made obligatory upon me and my community fifty prayers every day and night. I descended to Mūsā, and he said: Go back and ask your Lord for a reduction. I kept going back and forth between Mūsā and my Lord until my Lord, Glorified and Exalted, said: O Muhammad, they are five prayers, each prayer counting as ten, so that is fifty prayers. I descended to Mūsā, and he said: Go back and ask Him for a reduction. I said: I have become ashamed before my Lord." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from his journey and informed Quraysh; they called him a liar and asked him for descriptions of Bayt al-Maqdis, and his Lord displayed it for him, so he began describing it precisely. They asked him about a caravan of theirs, and he told them about it, and said: it will arrive on such-and-such a day, with the rising of the sun, led by a grey camel. On the appointed day, the disbelievers of Mecca went out to meet the caravan; one of them said: Here is the sun, it has risen; and another said: Here is the caravan, it has come, led by a grey camel. That only increased them in obstinacy and arrogance. Some people tried to shake the faith of Abū Bakr, and he said: By Allah, I would believe him in something greater than that.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, and the second is relative: the fāʿil (agent) of (رأى) is a pronoun referring back to the Prophet ﷺ, and the returning pronoun is omitted, being a pronoun indicating the form of Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: It was said that it is the Essence of Allah the Exalted, with disagreement among the views about these sayings between the hadiths narrated from ʿĀʾisha and those narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.]» ...
The clause «ما كذب الفؤاد ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «رأى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative; (الفاء) conjunction; (على ما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تمارونه) by making it include the meaning of تغلبونه (you contend to overcome him). The clause «تمارونه ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. do you deny his word and dispute with him; and the clause «يرى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:13-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (نزلة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being of the kind expressing number «[Note: Or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he saw him descending another time.]» , (عند) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رآه), (عندها) an adverb attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (جنّة). The clause «رآه ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «عندها جنّة ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from سدرة.]» 16- 18- (إذ) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (رأى), (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of the first (يغشى), and the fāʿil of the second (يغشى) is a pronoun, which is the one returning to ما; (ما) negative in the two places; (لقد رأى) like لقد رآه; (من آيات) attached to (رأى), and (من) is partitive «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from الكبرى, which is the object of رأى.]» .
The clause «يغشى السدرة ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «يغشى (the second) has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); the clause «ما زاغ البصر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of رآه.]» ; the clause «ما طغى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما زاغ البصر; and the clause «رأى ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(13) نزلة: a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra) from the triliteral (نزل); its wazn is فعْلة, with fatḥa then sukūn. (14) المنتهى: a noun of place from the five-letter verb انتهى; its wazn is مفتعَل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; it may also be intended as the passive participle, i.e. the place to which one ends up.
(16) يغشى: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is يغشي — with yāʾ at its end — its past being غشي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif and became يغشى. (17) زاغ: it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is زيغ, its imperfect يزيغ; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Benefits:
- The nouns of time and place ...
They are two nouns indicating the time or place of the action ...
1- They are formed from the triliteral, when its ʿayn has fatḥa or ḍamma in the imperfect, on the wazn مفعَل, such as: شرب يشرب: مشرب. كتب يكتب: مكتب. Attached to this wazn is the triliteral with a weak final letter, such as: أوى يأوي: مأوى, as in the verse we are dealing with; سعى يسعى: مسعى; جرى يجري: مجرى.
2- They are formed from the triliteral, when its ʿayn has kasra in the imperfect, on the wazn (مفعِل), such as نزل ينزل: منزل. غزل يغزل: مغزل. Attached to this wazn is the triliteral with a weak first letter and a sound final letter, such as: وعد يعد: موعد. وقف يقف: موقف.
3- They are formed from what exceeds three letters on the wazn of its imperfect, after replacing the imperfect prefix with mīm and giving fatḥa to the letter before the last: ازدحم يزدحم: مزدحم. استعمل يستعمل:
مستعمل.
4- Whether the form is a noun of time or of place is distinguished from the context of the meaning. For example, if you say: منطلق الطائرة الساعة الخامسة مساء "The plane's departure is at five in the evening", then منطلق is a noun of time; but if you say مجتمع المسافرين في المحطة "The travellers' gathering place is in the station", then مجتمع is a noun of place. As for the form of the nouns of time and place from what exceeds three letters, it is like the form of the passive participle, and they are distinguished from the context of the meaning.

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative; (الفاء) conjunction, to make the seeing follow upon what was mentioned of the greatness of Allah the Exalted; (الأخرى) a second naʿt (adjective) of مناة, accusative (manṣūb). The clause «رأيتم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. have you known the greatness of Allah and His power, and then seen al-Lāt ... how contemptible it is and not worthy of worship «[Note: The second object of (رأيتم) is omitted, its implied form being: how powerless it is.. and some construed it with His saying, the Exalted:
أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثى
[.....]]»

* Morphology:
(اللات), the name of an idol, and (الألف) and (اللام) in it are redundant and obligatory, like those in الذي and التي. As for the (التاء), there is disagreement about it: it is radical according to some, from (لات يليت) meaning he withheld or diminished ... and it is augmentative according to others, so the word is from (لوى يلوى) because they used to turn (yalwūna) their necks towards it, or yaltawūna, i.e. they devoted themselves to it; the origin of the word is لوية, whose final radical (lām) was deleted, so the alif is converted from a wāw; this is the view taken by al-Muʿjam.. Some said that al-Lāt is taken from Allah. (العزّى), the name of an idol; it is فُعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn, from al-ʿizz (might), i.e. it is the feminine of الأعزّ; it was also said that it is the name of a tree that used to be worshipped. (مناة), the name of a rock that used to be worshipped besides Allah, derived from the verb منى يمني, i.e. he poured, because the blood of sacrificial animals used to be poured at it ... so its alif on this view is a yāʾ ...
al-ʿUkbarī says: «Its alif is from yāʾ, as in your saying مني يمني when he determined; and it may be from wāw, from which is منوان ... its wazn is فعَلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām. (الثالثة), feminine of الثالث, a noun for the ordering of number, on the wazn فاعل. «[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of al-ʿUkbarī's quotation is missing in the source.]»

safi-cedvel:21-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذكر), (له الأنثى) like لكم الذكر.
The clause «لكم الذكر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «له الأنثى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one. 22- The reference in (تلك) is to the division understood from the interrogative; (إذا) a particle of response; (ضيزى) a naʿt (adjective) of قسمة, nominative (marfūʿ). The clause «تلك ... قسمة ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). 23- (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr), and (الواو) in (سمّيتموها) is redundant, a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm, and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: I.e. you named the idols with them.]» (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, tawkīd (emphasis) for the fāʿil (agent) of سمّيتم; (آباؤكم) conjoined to the agent pronoun by the wāw, nominative; (ما) negative; (بها) attached to (أنزل) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. for their worship; (سلطان) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi; (إن, إلّا) like the two previous ones; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to الظنّ by (الواو), the returning pronoun being omitted; (الواو) resumptive; (لقد جاءهم) like لقد رآه «[Note: In verse (13) of this sura.]» , (من ربّهم) attached to (جاءهم) «[Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الهدى.]» .
The clause «إن هي إلّا أسماء ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; the clause «سمّيتموها ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of أسماء; the clause «ما أنزل اللَّه بها ... » is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of أسماء «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (سمّيتموها).]» ; the clause «إن يتّبعون إلّا الظن ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption; the clause «تهوى الأنفس ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); and the clause «جاءهم ... الهدى» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ضيزى), meaning unjust. The word is either a derived adjective on the wazn فُعلى — with ḍamma on the fāʾ, then given kasra to suit the yāʾ — or a maṣdar like ذكرى used as a description. Its verb is ضاز يضيز in judgment, meaning he was unjust; and ضازه فيه يضوزه, meaning he diminished and defrauded him, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب ... al-ʿUkbarī said: «ضيزى: its origin is ضوزى, like طوبى; its first letter was given kasra, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ; it is not originally on فِعلى — with kasra on the fāʾ —» And in al-Qāmūs and Tāj al-ʿArūs it is both wāw-based and yāʾ-based, so there is no conversion in it.

* Rhetoric:
The art of rhymed prose (fann al-sajʿ): in His saying, the Exalted, «قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزى» .
There is a marvellous art in the word «ضيزى». The ignorant may wonder about the secret of using the word «ضيزى», which is uncouth and unfamiliar. In fact, the use of words has secrets, and this word which the Noble Quran used has a marvellous secret in its use: nothing else can fill its place. Do you not see that the whole sura, Sūrat al-Najm, is rhymed on the letter yāʾ? He the Exalted said: «وَالنَّجْمِ إِذا هَوى ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ وَما غَوى», and so on to the end of the sura. When He mentioned the idols and the division of offspring, and what the disbelievers used to claim, He said: ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى. So this word came on the rhyming letter on which the whole sura came, and nothing else can fill its place. And since the aim was to deride their saying, to carry out «[Translator's note: the text reads تنفيذ (carrying out), probably a misprint for تفنيد (refuting).]» their division, and to denounce it, a word suited to derision and denunciation was chosen for it, as though the baseness of the word pointed to the baseness of their understanding.
This is among the most wondrous instances in the Noble Quran of words matching the requirements of the situation.

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza that is for denial; (للإنسان) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ما), the relative noun, the returning pronoun being omitted; (الفاء) causal; (اللَّه) «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently (للَّه) is meant.]» attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الآخرة) ...
The clause «للإنسان ما تمنّى ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «تمنّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); and the clause «للَّه الآخرة ... » has no grammatical position, being causal.

* Morphology:
(تمنّى), it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is تمنّي; the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كم) the declarative kam (khabariyya), meaning "many", in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (من ملك) the tamyīz (specification) of كم; (في السموات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of ملك; (لا) negative; (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is of the kind of the description, i.e. anything of availing; (إلّا) for exception; (من بعد) attached to a naʿt which is the implied (muqaddar) excepted, i.e. except an intercession after He permits; (أن) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأذن) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (لمن) attached to (يأذن), and the fāʿil (agent) of (يشاء, يرضى) is a pronoun referring back to the Name of Majesty. The clause «كم من ملك ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «لا تغني شفاعتهم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (كم); the clause «يأذن اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن); the clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من); and the clause «يرضى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يشاء.

safi-cedvel:27-30.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative; (بالآخرة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون), (اللام) for emphasis; (تسمية) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they name the angels with the naming of the female.]» .
The clause «إنّ الذين لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); and the clause «يسمّون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. 28- (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) negative; (لهم) attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (به) attached to a ḥāl from علم; (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (إن) negative; (إلا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (لا) negative; (من الحقّ) attached to (يغني) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from (شيئا).]» by making it include the meaning of يفيد (benefits); (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being of the kind of the description, i.e. an availing neither little nor much ...
The clause «ما لهم به من علم ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; the clause «إن يتّبعون إلّا الظن ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); the clause «انّ الظن لا يغني ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and the clause «لا يغني من الحقّ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. 29- (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (عمّن) attached to (أعرض), (عن ذكرنا) attached to (تولّى), (إلّا) for restriction. The clause «أعرض ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if they follow conjecture, which is other than the truth, then turn away from them; the clause «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من); and the clause «لم يرد إلّا الحياة ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause. 30- The reference in (ذلك) is to seeking the world; (من العلم) attached to the khabar (مبلغهم); (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative, its khabar being (أعلم), (بمن) attached to (أعلم); (عن سبيله) attached to (ضلّ), (هو أعلم بمن اهتدى) like هو أعلم بمن ضلّ. The clause «ذلك مبلغهم ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical; the clause «إنّ ربّك ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of the command to turn away; the clause «هو أعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna; the clause «ضلّ ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative noun (من); the clause «هو أعلم (the second) » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause هو أعلم (the first); and the clause «اهتدى» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(27) يسمون: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by deletion: the final radical of the verb, the yāʾ, was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural. (27) تسمية: a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb سمّى, and the tāʾ at its end is a substitute for the yāʾ of تفعيل, because yāʾ is the final radical of the word. (29) عن من: its writing in the Muṣḥaf came separated, while the analogy of the orthographic rule requires it to be joined (عمّن). (30) مبلغهم: a mīm-maṣdar from the triliteral بلغ; its wazn is مفعَل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn ... or it is a noun of place if what is intended by it is the degree reached in knowledge, knowledge being in degrees.
(اهتدى), the analogy of the iʿlāl in it is like (هدى) ... see verse (82) of Sūrat Ṭāhā.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (للَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) (ما), (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (ما في الأرض) conjoined to ما في السموات; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (يجزي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring back to the Name of Majesty; (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause is the ṣila.]» , the second (يجزي) is conjoined to the first, accusative; (بالحسنى) attached to the second (يجزي). The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزي ... ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being ملك «[Note: Or attached to (أعلم بمن ضلّ.. وبمن اهتدى), and the lām according to al-Zamakhsharī is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), not the lām of causation.]» , and the interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يجزي).
